meta.purpose: Reference facts for src/compat.js and src/physics.js (goggle/air-unit compatibility, RC interoperability, per-class defaults, battery and connector rules).
meta.conventions: Weights in grams. Fields listed in an entry's `est` array are estimates or derived values, not published specs. 'ship' weights quoted from store catalogs are Shopify shipping weights (rounded), used only as an upper bound.
meta.verification: Adversarial re-check 2026-10-19 against dji.com (O4 specs/FAQ, Goggles 3 and N3 FAQs), caddxfpv.com (Walksnail kit and goggle pages), hd-zero.com (Race V3, Freestyle V2), expresslrs.org, frsky-rc.com, fpvknowitall.com, and the RaceDayQuads / NewBeeDrone / Five33 product text captured in .scratch/index. getfpv.com refused automated fetches (HTTP 403), so claims that rested only on GetFPV were either re-sourced, softened or removed; see per-entry notes.

analog.label: Analog 5.8 GHz
goggles_native: Skyzone SKY04X Pro (built-in 48CH V3.3 Steadyview receiver)
Skyzone SKY04O Pro (48CH receiver module included)
Skyzone Cobra X V4 (48CH diversity receiver module included)
Fat Shark Dominator HDO 2.1 (sold with Fat Shark 32CH 5.8 GHz receiver module)
EMAX Transporter 2 (built-in 5.8 GHz receiver, box goggles)

goggles_with_module_or_firmware.requirement: HDZero Analog Expansion Module V2 plus a Fat Shark-style analog receiver module (e.g. ImmersionRC rapidFIRE, TBS Fusion); the expansion module is sold without a receiver
Optional: its add-on analog module bay accepts most analog modules for better reception than the built-in receiver

goggles_with_module_or_firmware.goggles: Fat Shark Dominator HDO+ (sold without a receiver)
goggles_with_module_or_firmware.requirement: Analog receiver module in the RF module bay (3.5 mm AV in also available)
External analog receiver into the AV/CVBS input (Caddx: 'Supports HDMI, AV, and CVBS video input')

Fat Shark-style analog module on an adapter that feeds the goggles' AV input (e.g. 'Analog FPV FatShark Module Adapter V3 for DJI Digital FPV Goggles'). Note: the Flywoo 1G2-1G3 VRX sold for DJI FPV Goggles V2 is a 1.2/1.3 GHz receiver and does not receive 5.8 GHz analog
Analog module in the module bay (e.g. ImmersionRC rapidFIRE with Orqa receiver module, natively integrated)
Analog receiver module in the modular receiver bay

caveats: DJI Goggles 3 and DJI Goggles N3 do not support analog video (both FAQs answer 'No'). DJI Goggles 2 and Integra list no analog input on the pages checked.
Walksnail Avatar HD Goggles L list no AV input or module bay (I/O is a 4-pin 3.5 mm plug, DC 5.5x2.1 mm and microSD only).
Fat Shark Dominator HD (Walksnail-based) has no analog module ('There is not an analog Module for these', RDQ Q&A).
HDZero goggles 'sometimes glitch out when analog signal is weak' (fpvknowitall).
HDZero goggles and the Analog Expansion Module add a real-time deinterlacer for analog input; analog camera latency is listed as 3 ms on BoxPro/BoxPro+.

hdzero.label: HDZero
goggles_native: EMAX Transporter 2 HD (designed with HDZero; 720p 60 Hz screen)

goggles_with_module_or_firmware.goggles: Any goggles with HDMI input (e.g. Skyzone SKY04X Pro, Walksnail Avatar HD Goggles X)
goggles_with_module_or_firmware.requirement: HDZero VRX4 receiver module feeding the goggles' HDMI input (RDQ: 'Compatible with any goggles using HDMI input')

caveats: All HDZero VTXs released to date work with all HDZero goggles released to date (fpvknowitall).

Two camera interfaces: MIPI VTXs (Race V3, Freestyle V2, Whoop V2, Whoop Lite) take MIPI cameras (Nano V3, Nano 90, Micro V3); the ECO VTX and HDZero AIO boards take the single-wire HD-composite cameras (ECO, Lux). A regular analog camera works with neither.
Modes: 540p90 / 720p60 / 1080p30 on Race V3 and Whoop V2; Freestyle V2 adds 540p60. Glass-to-glass latency ~3 ms on Goggle 2; BoxPro lists 4 ms with HDZero cameras.

Whoop V2 VTX: no reverse-polarity protection; needs >=1.5 A from a 5 V pad; direct 1S power can dip below 3 V on punch-outs and drop video; add an external capacitor on 3S. Race V3 has reverse-polarity protection.
No DJI interoperability; Walksnail is viewable on HDZero goggles only through a Walksnail VRX's HDMI output.

dji-o4.label: DJI O4 (O4 Air Unit / 'O4 Lite')

goggles_with_module_or_firmware.requirement: Update firmware; DJI RC must be FPV Remote Controller 2; no Racing Mode (Goggles 3/N3 only) and max 40 MHz channel bandwidth (60 MHz listed only for Goggles 3/N3); latency <35 ms at 1080p/100fps
Update firmware; DJI RC must be FPV Remote Controller 2; no Racing Mode and max 40 MHz channel bandwidth; latency <35 ms at 1080p/100fps

caveats: Not compatible with DJI FPV Goggles V1/V2 (not listed by DJI) or any third-party goggles (DJI O4 FAQ: 'Third-party flight goggles are not supported').
Racing Mode needs Goggles 3 or N3. N3 has a 60 Hz screen and ~4 ms more latency than G3/G2/Integra (fpvknowitall; DJI lists 20 ms on G3 vs 24 ms on N3).
Rated 3.7-13.2 V, but fpvknowitall reports dropout around 3.8 V; on 1S it needs a step-up regulator or it 'will die out about halfway through the pack'.
FC firmware for OSD: Betaflight 4.3.0+ or INAV 8.0.1+. Using the DJI FPV Remote Controller needs the FC receiver protocol set to SBUS; other radios need a separate receiver.
Above 25 C ambient DJI recommends external cooling and heat-conductive material to the frame; when hot the bitrate drops to a maximum of 50 Mbps.

Camera module (13.44 x 12.36 x 16.50 mm) and transmission module differ from O3 (DJI FAQ: O4 cannot be installed directly on O3 frames); use O4-specific mounts, adapter plates or 18/20 mm camera shells.
No aftermarket cameras exist for O3/O4 air units (fpvknowitall); third-party products are lens or shell swaps (e.g. Flywoo O4 Wide 159 deg lens).

dji-o4-pro.label: DJI O4 Pro (O4 Air Unit Pro)

goggles_with_module_or_firmware.requirement: Update firmware; DJI RC must be FPV Remote Controller 2; no Racing Mode; latency <30 ms at 1080p/100fps
Update firmware; DJI RC must be FPV Remote Controller 2; no Racing Mode; latency <30 ms at 1080p/100fps

caveats: Not compatible with DJI FPV Goggles V1/V2 or third-party goggles.

Camera is 20 mm wide but 25.55 mm deep and 23.3 mm tall - 'very large and doesn't fit into most frames unless they have been specifically adapted' (fpvknowitall). DJI/RDQ: fits frames of 3 inches and above.
Input 7.4-26.4 V (2S-6S); 8S-12S builds need a separate regulator. 2T2R with two antennas (~2.1 g each).
Same SBUS requirement for the DJI FPV Remote Controller and same Betaflight 4.3.0+/INAV 8.0.1+ requirement as O4.

dji-o3.label: DJI O3 Air Unit

goggles_with_module_or_firmware.requirement: Goggles 3 firmware v01.00.0300 or later and current O3 firmware (RDQ Goggles 3 listing). DJI lists Goggles 3 with FPV Remote Controller 3; the RC pairing for O3-on-G3 was not stated on the pages checked
Listed as compatible with the O3 camera module and air unit; update goggles and air unit firmware; live view up to 810p/120fps with latency <28 ms (810p/60fps <40 ms)

caveats: DJI Goggles N3 do NOT support O3 (N3 FAQ lists only Avata 2, Neo and the O4 series; fpvknowitall: 'the N3 does NOT support the O3 air unit at this time').

Power: GetFPV's listing says the O3 'can draw close to 2A' (GetFPV not re-fetchable, HTTP 403); FC makers size dedicated O3 rails at 10 V 2-2.5 A (Holybro Kakute G4 AIO, NewBeeDrone BeeBrain). Use a 9-10 V BEC rated >=2 A or power the unit from the battery.
Receives on 2.4 and 5.8 GHz but transmits only on 5.8 GHz.
Records 4K at 50/60 fps and 2.7K/1080p up to 100 fps (120 fps with DJI FPV Goggles V2) to 20 GB internal storage.
Pairs with the DJI FPV Remote Controller 2 (Goggles 2/Integra/FPV Goggles V2); FC receiver protocol must be SBUS.

dji-v1.label: DJI FPV System V1 (DJI FPV Air Unit, Caddx Vista, RunCam Link)

goggles_with_module_or_firmware.requirement: Firmware update; fpvknowitall: 'the G2 is compatible with the Vista-generation air units'

caveats: DJI Goggles 3 and N3 FAQs list only O3/O4-generation products - treat V1 air units as incompatible with them.
DJI Goggles Integra compatibility with V1 air units is not stated on the pages checked.
Vista: 720p/120fps low-latency mode 21-28 ms; FCC/SRRC range 4 km (CE 0.7 km); input 7.4-26.4 V; built-in receiver for the original DJI FPV Remote Controller.
Legacy system: V1-generation kits are discontinued/out of stock at the stores checked.

walksnail.label: Walksnail Avatar
goggles_native: Fat Shark Recon HD (Walksnail-compatible box goggles, 1080p 60 fps)

goggles_with_module_or_firmware.requirement: Walksnail Avatar VRX feeding the HDMI input (VRX outputs 720p100; BoxPro lists 100 Hz HDMI input with 1 ms latency)
Walksnail Avatar VRX feeding HDMI IN (listed as 720P 100FPS)
Walksnail Avatar VRX (HDMI out 1080p60 / 720p100 / 720p60, 7-25.2 V input, ~83 g)

caveats: All Walksnail Avatar goggles are compatible with all Avatar VTXs (fpvknowitall; Goggles X page: 'Fully compatible with all Walksnail VTX Kits'). Older goggles may need a firmware update for newer VTXs (RDQ review of Dominator HD with Nano V3).
Walksnail ASCENT is a separate system: Ascent goggles are 'Not compatible with Avatar systems', so Ascent and Avatar do not mix.
Goggles L: 60 Hz LCD, 1080p60/720p60 only, no native aftermarket-antenna support and no AV input.
Avatar Pro / Nano V3 kit listings: Walksnail recommends a standalone BEC between VTX and power source above 2S.
Mini 1S VTX runs 3.1-13 V on V3 hardware (3.1-5 V on V2) but 'drops out HARD at 3.1 volts' (fpvknowitall).
GT/GT2 VTX need 11.1-25.2 V (3S-6S) and are physically larger (GT2 34 x 36 x 23.5 mm with fan).

openipc.label: OpenIPC (open-source WiFi-based HD)

goggles_with_module_or_firmware.goggles: Goggles with HDMI input (e.g. HDZero Goggle 2 / BoxPro, Skyzone SKY04X Pro, Walksnail Goggles X)
goggles_with_module_or_firmware.requirement: OpenIPC ground receiver with HDMI out: EMAX Wyvern Link Goggle VRX (DC 8-24 V; EMAX advertises attachment to Fat Shark-style goggles) or RunCam WiFiLink-RX (9-30 V, HDMI 1080p60/720p60)

caveats: No goggles receive OpenIPC natively; the Wyvern ground VRX 'Works only with OpenIPC VTX and display, not standalone' and must be paired with an OpenIPC VTX.
EMAX Wyvern Link hardware is sold as an Alpha release.
RunCam WiFiLink 2 quotes ~40 ms latency; RunCam WiFiLink-RX also supports Ruby FPV.
Configuration is done over Ethernet/USB-C adapters (EMAX) or a network card (RunCam) - more setup than DJI/Walksnail/HDZero.

air_units.name: DJI O4 Air Unit (O4 Lite)
air_units.records: 4K60 (1080p up to 120fps), 100 Mbps, 23 GB internal, no microSD
air_units.notes: 8.2 g with camera + 0.75 g antenna (DJI: 9.2 g with lens mount). Camera module 13.44 x 12.36 x 16.50 mm - sits in 14 mm nano slots with O4 adapter plates/cases. Transmission module 30 x 30 x 6 mm; RDQ lists a 25.5 x 25.5 mm mounting pattern (DJI's FAQ loosely says '30 x 30 mm' hole distance). Practical dropout ~3.8 V. DJI publishes no power figure.

air_units.name: Flywoo DJI O4 Wide Air Unit Set (159 deg lens)
air_units.records: 4K60, max 60 Mbps live bitrate, 23 GB internal, no microSD
air_units.notes: DJI O4 internals with a Flywoo 159 deg lens; 13 g including camera and 50 mm coax; 80 mm copper-tube antenna; ships with 18 mm and 20 mm camera shells so the 14 mm camera fits micro/O3-style mounts. Input range not on the listing (taken from the DJI O4).

air_units.name: DJI O4 Air Unit Pro
air_units.records: 4K120 (16:9; 4K 4:3 up to 60fps; 2.7K/1080p modes), 130 Mbps, D-Log M, 4 GB internal + microSD up to 512 GB
air_units.notes: 32 g with camera (15.6 g without) + 2 x 2.1 g antennas. Camera 25.55 x 20 x 23.30 mm. Transmission module 33.5 x 33.5 x 13 mm. DJI publishes no power figure.

air_units.name: DJI O3 Air Unit
air_units.notes: 36.4 g with camera (camera module 8.3 g incl. coax) + two stock antennas at ~3 g each. Camera fits 20 mm mounts (frames list '20mm (DJI and O3 camera)'). Air-unit side of NewBeeDrone's O3 adapter is 25.5 x 25.5. GetFPV says it 'can draw close to 2A' - size the 9-10 V BEC for 2 A (peak ~18 W); typical draw is lower.

air_units.name: Caddx Vista (DJI FPV V1)
air_units.notes: Figures are for the Caddx Nebula Pro Vista Kit (the previous 29 g figure for the DJI-camera Vista came only from GetFPV, which could not be re-fetched): 25 g with camera + 1.5 g antenna; Vista board 30 x 29 x 13 mm; Nebula Pro camera 19 x 19 x 20 mm. 720p120, 25/200/500/700 mW, no onboard recording (records in goggles). Discontinued. 20 x 20 pattern inferred from frames/VTXs sold as Vista-compatible (e.g. HDZero Freestyle V2, 20x20 M2).

air_units.name: Walksnail Avatar HD Pro Kit (dual antenna)
air_units.notes: VTX 15.4 g + Pro camera 9.5 g + 2 x 2 g antennas = 28.9 g (marketing copy says 'Weighing only 30g'). Camera 19 x 19 x 24 mm (1/1.8in Starvis II). Walksnail recommends a standalone BEC above 2S.

air_units.name: Walksnail Avatar HD Kit V2 (dual antenna)
air_units.notes: VTX 15.4 g + camera 7.2 g + 2 x 2 g antennas (2x IPEX) = 26.6 g. Camera 19 x 19 x 22 mm, 1/3.2in 4 MP 4:3 sensor.

air_units.name: Walksnail Avatar Moonlight Kit (4K)
air_units.notes: Gross 38.5 g without antennas + 2 x 2 g antennas = 42.5 g (camera 8.9 g without wire, recording board 10 g). Camera 19.6 x 19 x 24 mm. VTX 15.3 x 34.5 x 34.5 mm. Listed draw 12 V x 1.4 A (8 V x 2.2 A).

air_units.name: Walksnail Avatar GT Kit (2 W)
air_units.records: 1080p / 720p to microSD (up to 256 GB, not included)
air_units.notes: VTX 41.6 g incl. antenna + Pro camera 9.5 g. Up to 2 W output; heatsink-cooled (fan sold separately). No published power figure.

air_units.name: Walksnail Avatar GT2 Kit (2 W)
air_units.notes: 52 g WITHOUT antenna (antenna weight not published on the listing); VTX 34 x 36 x 23.5 mm with cooling fan; camera 19 x 19 x 24 mm; JST1.0 6-pin power cable; head-tracking support with compatible goggles/gimbals.

air_units.name: Walksnail Avatar HD Nano Kit V3 (Mini VTX V3 + Nano Camera V3)
air_units.notes: Kit 18.5 g: metal-cased Mini VTX V3 13.4 g (31.5 x 31.5 x 9.4 mm) + Nano Camera V3 3 g (14 x 14 x 16.8 mm) + antenna. 500 mW. Mounting 25.5 x 25.5 (M2 holes) and 20 x 20 (M3 holes). Walksnail recommends a standalone BEC above 2S.

air_units.name: Walksnail Avatar HD Mini 1S Kit (V3)
air_units.records: 1080p / 720p, 8 GB internal (Caddx page; some store variants list 32 GB)
air_units.notes: VTX 6.8 g + nano camera 3.5 g (14 x 14 x 17 mm) + 2 g antenna. 500 mW. V2 VTX was 3.1-5 V only. Hard dropout at 3.1 V.

air_units.name: Walksnail Avatar HD Mini 1S Lite Kit
air_units.notes: Kit 7.8 g (camera 1.8 g, 14 x 14 x 16 mm; antenna 0.5 g). Input 3.1-13 V on V3 hardware, 3.1-5 V on V2 - check the board version before powering above 5 V. Page lists the VTX as 5.1 g in prose and 6.8 g in the spec table.

air_units.name: HDZero Race V3 VTX
air_units.notes: 25/200 mW, 540p90/720p60/1080p30, reverse-polarity protection, 1.6 mm PCB, 32 x 28 x 5 mm. Mounting 20 x 20 with M4 holes and rubber grommets. MIPI camera sold separately (see hdzero_cameras). Power draw not published; Whoop Lite (same generation) is 5.8 W at 200 mW.

air_units.name: HDZero Freestyle V2 VTX
air_units.notes: Published draw 6-15 W (15 W used as the max). 25/200 mW, up to 1 W on R1 when unlocked with a licence. 720p60/1080p30/540p60/540p90. 29 x 30 x 14 mm; fits most Vista/RunCam Link frames. Kit adds Nano 90 camera (5.2 g without cable, 14 mm wide, ships with a 19 x 19 mount).

air_units.name: HDZero Whoop V2 VTX
air_units.notes: Published draw 5-6 W; 25/200 mW; 1S-3S; 5.4 g (5.1 g without wires); no reverse-polarity protection; MIPI cameras only.

air_units.name: HDZero Whoop Lite VTX
air_units.notes: 4.9 g with wires (4.6 g without; NewBeeDrone comparison table); RDQ lists 4.5 g without shielding. 5 W at 25 mW, 5.8 W at 200 mW (RDQ; NewBeeDrone lists 7 W). 1S-3S; MIPI cameras.

air_units.name: HDZero ECO VTX + ECO camera
air_units.notes: NewBeeDrone ECO Bundle: VTX ~4.5 g + camera ~1.6 g with wire + 0.2 g dipole = ~6.3 g (fpvknowitall says 'about 7-8 grams'). 1S-3S input, 25/200 mW, 25 x 25 M2 soft mount. HD-composite single-wire camera link: takes the ECO or Lux camera, not MIPI cameras.

air_units.name: EMAX Wyvern Link OpenIPC 200 mW VTX
air_units.notes: IMX415, 1080p90 / 720p120, 2-6S. Includes camera, USB-C/Ethernet adapter and two dipoles. Camera size not published: the identically weighted Wyvern Link (Alpha) 100 mW VTX lists a 14 mm lens module, the 800 mW versions 19 mm - check before choosing a camera mount.

air_units.name: EMAX Wyvern Link Alpha V2 800 mW VTX (aluminum case)
air_units.notes: 48.2 g incl. 19 x 19 mm IMX415 camera (excl. antenna cable); 2-6S; active fan cooling; 1080p90 / 720p120.

air_units.name: RunCam WiFiLink 2 (OpenIPC)
air_units.notes: IMX415, 1080p60/1080p90/720p120, ~40 ms latency, 19 x 19 mm M12 lens module on 130 mm MIPI cable, PCB 30.6 x 33 mm. Weight not on the listing (the earlier RunCam WiFiLink / WiFiLink-G list 30 g).

hdzero_cameras.name: RunCam HDZero Nano V3
hdzero_cameras.notes: Listed L14 x W16 x H14 mm; MIPI cable not included

hdzero_cameras.name: RunCam HDZero Lux
hdzero_cameras.notes: Listed L14 x W16 x H14 mm; for the ECO VTX and HDZero AIO boards (aspect ratio set manually on both), not MIPI VTXs

hdzero_cameras.name: RunCam HDZero Eco
hdzero_cameras.notes: 14 x 14 x 13 mm, 1.8 g with cable (ECO Bundle text says 1.6 g); for the ECO VTX and HDZero AIO boards

hdzero_cameras.name: RunCam HDZero Nano 90 (V1/V2)
hdzero_cameras.notes: L18 x W14 x H18 mm, 5.2 g without cable; the Freestyle V2 kit ships it with a 19 x 19 mount; V2 changed the lens (FOV D162)

hdzero_cameras.name: HDZero Micro V3
hdzero_cameras.notes: 19 x 19 x 24 mm; MIPI cable not included

elrs-2.4.label: ExpressLRS 2.4 GHz
elrs-2.4.notes: ELRS FAQ: 'Any Receiver and TX Module from the same Band ... will work together', across manufacturers, if both run the same major ELRS version (binding page: 'The first number in the Version string should match') and the same binding phrase/regulatory domain. A Gemini Xrossband/dual-band TX (e.g. RadioMaster Nomad Dual) can also run single-band 2.4 GHz modes, and LR1121 multi-frequency receivers (XR1: 'ISM 2.4 or FCC 915') can run 2.4 GHz. 2.4 GHz hardware does not talk to 900 MHz-only hardware. Single-band Gemini needs a true-diversity receiver.

elrs-900.label: ExpressLRS 900 MHz (868/915)
elrs-900.notes: Same rules as 2.4: same band + same major version + same configuration (FAQ cites Regulatory Domain, so FCC 915 and EU 868 hardware must be set alike). Dual-band TX modules can run single-band 868/900 MHz modes.

elrs-dual.label: ExpressLRS Gemini Xrossband (2.4 GHz + 900 MHz)
elrs-dual.notes: GemX is available to devices with 2 LR1121 RF chipsets; X-modes (X100 Full Res, X150) run one RF circuit on sub-GHz and the other on 2.4 GHz and lock antenna mode to Gemini. 'A GemX-capable receiver will be required for this mode, and any single-band receiver will not get a sync' - the TX must be switched to a single-band packet rate. In ELRS 4.0 the TX module changes mode automatically to match the receiver in sync. Major versions must match.

crossfire.label: TBS Crossfire (868/915 MHz)
crossfire.notes: Proprietary TBS link; receivers output CRSF to the FC. Crossfire TX modules bind only Crossfire receivers - Tracer is a different 2.4 GHz product line. CRSF on the FC side is shared with ELRS/Tracer (same serial protocol), but the RF links do not interoperate.

tracer.label: TBS Tracer (2.4 GHz)
tracer.notes: 'Next generation of crossfire with 2.4GHz technology' - same CRSF/SBUS outputs to the FC, but a different band from Crossfire, so Tracer TX binds only Tracer receivers.

ghost.label: ImmersionRC Ghost (2.4 GHz)
ghost.notes: Ghost receivers bind to Ghost (JR-bay) transmitters; FC output SBUS, SBUS-Fast, SRXL-2 or GHST.

frsky-access.label: FrSky ACCESS
frsky-access.notes: FrSky: 'users can bind the ACCST D16 receivers with a new ACCESS transmitter'. D8 (and LR12) receivers need an external XJT / XJT Lite module. ACCESS is not supported by the 4-in-1 multiprotocol module.

frsky-accst.label: FrSky ACCST D16
frsky-accst.notes: D16 exists as v1 (FrSkyX) and v2.1 (FrSkyX2) firmware families, each in FCC and EU-LBT flavours - TX and RX firmware family/flavour must match. A 4-in-1 multiprotocol module (CC2500) speaks both D16 v1 and D16 v2.1.

frsky-d8.label: FrSky D8
frsky-d8.notes: Older 8-channel FrSky protocol (D4R/D8R era). Supported by the 4-in-1 multiprotocol module (CC2500, protocol FrskyD). ACCESS radios need an external XJT/XJT Lite module for D8.

flysky-afhds2a.label: FlySky AFHDS 2A
flysky-afhds2a.notes: Supported by the 4-in-1 multiprotocol module (A7105 chip, protocol AFHDS2A).

flysky-afhds3.label: FlySky AFHDS 3
flysky-afhds3.notes: Not in the multiprotocol module's protocol list, so a 4-in-1 module cannot bind AFHDS 3 receivers. Treat AFHDS 3 and AFHDS 2A as separate links unless the radio lists both.

spektrum-dsmx.label: Spektrum DSMX
spektrum-dsmx.notes: Supported by the 4-in-1 multiprotocol module (CYRF6936 chip, protocol DSM covering DSM2/DSMX).

dji-rc.label: DJI FPV Remote Controller (via the air unit)
dji-rc.notes: The DJI air unit acts as the receiver and outputs SBUS - the FC's receiver protocol must be SBUS. FPV Remote Controller 3 with Goggles 3/N3 + O4; FPV Remote Controller 2 with Goggles 2/Integra + O3/O4 and with FPV Goggles V2 + O3. (O3 on Goggles 3 works after firmware v01.00.0300; DJI lists Goggles 3 with RC 3, but the O3-on-G3 RC pairing is not stated on the pages checked.) V1 air units (Vista etc.) have a built-in receiver for the original DJI FPV Remote Controller via DJI FPV Goggles. Walksnail, HDZero and OpenIPC have no equivalent - they need a separate receiver.

rc_multiprotocol_module.label: 4-in-1 multiprotocol module (MPM / RadioMaster 4IN1 / Jumper JP4IN1)
rc_multiprotocol_module.notes: 70+ protocols in total (DSMX, FlySky, SFHSS, Hitec, HoTT, Radiolink, FrSky ...). FrSky D16 v1 = FrSkyX, D16 v2.1 = FrSkyX2. ACCESS, AFHDS 3, Crossfire, ELRS and Ghost were not in the protocol list read.

w65.typical_battery: 1S 250-480 mAh LiHV, BT2.0 / PH2.0 / A30 / GNB27
w65.notes: Air65 II: 17.8 g dry + LAVA II 320 mAh 8.2 g = ~26 g, 5:00 flight, claimed 6.3:1 T/W. Meteor65 Pro II (O4 version listing): 36.2 g + 480 mAh 12.6 g = ~49 g, 4:05. fpvknowitall targets <20 g dry for 65 mm freestyle and notes ~4 g extra for HDZero (Mobula6 HDZero vs analog). Misc = BT2.0 pigtail, solder/wire, canopy screws, RX antenna (0.25-1 g).

w75.notes: Air75 II: 21.3 g + 480 mAh 12.6 g = ~34 g, 7:30. Meteor75 Pro II: 41.5 g + 580/680 mAh = ~56 g, 5:00-6:00. AcroBee75 O4: 44 g dry on 2S 450-850 mAh XT30, ~3:00 on 450 mAh 2S. Pavo Femto (2S, O4): 54.77 g, T/W 'exceeds 6.75:1'.

p2.notes: Flytimes 85 O4: 58.9 g, 5:30 (550) / 7:30 (750) / 9:00 (1000 mAh) at 24-27% takeoff throttle. Flybee 20 O4: 47.6 g. Pavo Pico II O4: 53.7 g, up to 6:30. Aquila20: 127 g takeoff with 2S 1100 mAh, ~10 min. Firefly 20 Pro O4: 99 g on 4S 450-750, 5:00-6:30. DINO 20: 94 g on 3S 550-850, 5-11 min. M1103 motors make ~225-238 g thrust each.

p25.notes: Firefly 25 Mini O4: 99.5 g dry on 3S 550/750/1000 mAh -> 8:00 / 9:30 / 12:30 at 25-27% takeoff throttle. Pavo20 Pro II (2.2in, O4 Pro): under 150 g, up to 6:30, T/W 'greater than 5:1'. fpvknowitall: 2.5in props are less efficient/thrusty than 3in. F1204 5000KV + 2.5in prop: ~157 g thrust per motor on 3S.

p3.typical_battery: 3S 380-500 mAh or 4S 650-850 mAh (XT30); 6S 550 mAh on some
p3.notes: Baby Ape Pro V3: 74.1 g, 5-7 min on 3S 380 mAh. Cinelog30 V3 (O4 Pro): 187 g on 4S 660-720 mAh, 8:10 cruising. AvantQuads Avio 3: ~100 g dry analog / 125 g DJI plus ~100 g battery; 3in freestyle often 230-250 g (fpvknowitall). F1404: 301-480 g thrust per motor depending on KV/voltage. LionBee 3in LR on a 1S 18650: 62.3 g net, ~15 min flight / ~20 min hover (outlier).

p35.notes: Sub-250 3.5in builds land ~225-250 g with 4S 850 (~100 g) (fpvknowitall; 1404 motors standard). Manta 3.6: 108 g dry, 'over 8-minute' flight. CineApe 35 O3: 309 g on 6S 1300-1500, 7 min with GoPro / 9.5 min without. Axisflying C35 V3 O4 Pro: 385 g on 6S 1050-2200. Rekon35 V2: 174 g, 2S with built-in charging, up to 15 min (long-range outlier).

p4.notes: Flywoo Explorer LR 4 V2: ~162 g dry; spec table says ~229 g with 4S 750 mAh (listing intro says ~246 g); 4S1P 18650 3000 mAh packs weigh ~208 g (Auline V45) -> ~370 g, and Flywoo claims 'up to 28 minutes of cruising' on them. Upper flight-time bound is that Li-ion cruising claim.

p5.notes: fpvknowitall: 5in freestyle is 'almost always' 6S, ~1100-1400 mAh / 180-220 g packs. Vapor X5 O4 Pro: 409 g + 6S 1300-1800. BOB46: 455 g, 697 g takeoff with 6S 1480. Max thrust per 2207: 1711 g (Axisflying 2207.5 1860KV) to 2136 g (T-Motor F50) -> static T/W ~9-13 at 650 g; in-flight lower due to sag. GetFPV: a 1300 mAh 4S racer lasts ~3 min. Misc breakdown: XT60 pigtail ~8 g (XT60H 3.5 g + 14AWG lead), strap 3-7.5 g, capacitor 2-5 g, TPU 5-10 g, antennas/mounts 1-3 g, wire/solder/zip ties ~3 g.

p6.notes: Nazgul Evoque F6D V2 (O4 Pro, GPS): 485 g, ~710 g takeoff with 6S 1480, max hover ~8.5 min. Vapor-D6: 465 g on 6S 1500-2000 (listing claims 14-19 min). 6in 'should have slightly longer flight times' than 5in (fpvknowitall).

p7.typical_battery: 6S 2600-4500 mAh LiPo or 6S 6000-8000 mAh Li-ion, XT60
p7.notes: Crocodile75 V3 (O3): 628.5 g on 6S LiPo 2600-4200 or Li-ion 6000, 12-30 min. iFlight CineLR 7 (O4 Pro): 770 g dry, ~1628 g takeoff with 6S 8000 mAh 21700; hover ~18 min on 6S 3300 / ~25 min on 6S 8000. T-Motor F100 2810: 2467-2565 g max thrust per motor on 6S with 7in props.

p8.typical_battery: 6S 3000-6000 mAh Li-ion or LiPo, XT60 (XT90 on cinelifters)
p8.notes: Few complete 8in BNFs in the store catalogs. Built up from parts: frames 270-380 g (Mark4/Chimera9 class), 2810 1100KV with 8in props ~2600 g max thrust per motor; iFlight Centurion X8 cinelifter frame alone is 969 g. Values are estimates (not re-verified in this pass).

p10.typical_battery: 6S 5000-8000 mAh (LiPo 5600 or Li-ion 8000), XT60/XT90; 8S on some
p10.notes: iFlight Helion 10 (O4 Pro): 1072 g dry, ~1912 g takeoff with 6S 8000 mAh; hover ~26 min on 6S 5600 LiPo / ~30 min on 6S 8000 Li-ion; cruise 23-26 min; ships with an XT90 adapter. T-Motor V3115 900KV + 10in: 4605 g max thrust per motor at 23 V.

p13.notes: Estimates (not re-verified in this pass). X-class motors: iFlight XING X5215 330KV 356 g each, 4-8S, 76 A max; XING X4214 400KV. 13in props (Gemfan/HQ 13x8x3 to 13x12x3) on 25x25/30x30 M4 mounts with M6 shafts. Heavy-lift builds sit at the low T/W end, X-class racers at the high end. DJI O4 Pro/O3 input tops out at 26.4 V (6S): 8S-12S builds need a separate regulator for the air unit.

p15.notes: Estimates (not re-verified in this pass). iFlight iXC15 950 mm X-class frame 643 g (no TPU), 19x19-25x25 motor mounts. 4 x X5215 (356 g) = 1.4 kg of motors before props, ESCs, battery. Typical 8S 1300-1550 mAh packs weigh 240-330 g; larger packs for longer races. 8S+ exceeds every digital air unit's input range (max 26.4 V) - use a BEC.

notes: Battery strap: 3 g (Ethix V2 20x230, RDQ 180x10 Kevlar) to 7.5 g (Lumenier Kevlar 20x250).
XT60H connector: 3.5 g each (GetFPV listing, not re-fetchable); XT30 and capacitors ship at 1-5 g (store shipping weights).
Low-ESR capacitor 470-1000 uF 35-50 V: ~2-5 g.

5.8 GHz antennas: Lumenier AXII 2 U.FL 2.4 g, MMCX 3 g, right-angle stubby 6.7 g, Foxeer Lollipop V4 4.5 g; DJI O3 antenna ~3 g; DJI O4 antenna ~0.75 g; DJI O4 Pro antenna ~2.1 g; Walksnail V2 antenna 2 g; TBS Immortal T 2.4 GHz RX antenna 0.84 g; TrueRC Singularity 915 MHz SMA 24 g; tiny-whoop SMOL antenna 0.25 g.
Standoffs: HQ M3 1-2.5 g each; Matek M2 soft-mount 1.1 g each.
LiPo: 4.2 V full, 3.7 V nominal; LiHV: 4.35 V full, 3.8 V storage/nominal. LiHV gives more power early but drops off abruptly; LiPo discharge is more linear (GetFPV).

Land LiPo at a minimum of ~3.5 V/cell resting (3.65 V is safest) and store at 3.8 V/cell (GetFPV). Landing there leaves roughly 15-20% in the pack, hence the 0.8 usable-capacity rule of thumb (derived, not a published figure).

Li-ion 21700 cells: 3.6 V rated, 4.2 V charge cut-off, 2.5 V discharge cut-off, 70 A continuous / 120 A burst (Lumenier NAV listings). Flying Li-ion down to ~3.0 V/cell uses more of the capacity, so 0.85 usable; loaded voltage ~3.5 V/cell is an estimate below the 3.6 V rating.

C rating x capacity = theoretical max continuous current (GetFPV). Most packs can exceed it for ~10 s; GetFPV suggests 70C+ for 220-size quads and sizing so ~75% of max motor current fits the per-motor share.

LiPo C ratings are marketing: a 1300 mAh '150C (burst 250C)' pack implies 195 A continuous, more than 3x the 60 A rated current GetFPV lists for the XT60H connector it ships with. A common heuristic (used in compat.js) is to trust ~half the printed LiPo rating; that factor is a heuristic, not a published number.

Li-ion packs publish real amp limits instead of inflated C: 6S 4500 mAh 21700 S70 = 70 A continuous (~15.6C); 4S 3000 mAh 18650 V45 = 45 A continuous (208 g); Lumenier NAV 21700 cells 70 A continuous / 120 A burst.
HV packs wear faster than standard 4.20 V packs - charge right before flying and store at storage voltage (fpvknowitall).

Typical pack weight anchors: 1S 300 mAh ~8 g, 1S 480 mAh ~12.6 g, 2S 450 mAh ~28 g, 4S 850 mAh ~100-110 g, 6S 1300 mAh ~220 g, 4S1P 18650 3000 mAh ~208 g, 6S 4500 mAh Li-ion ~428 g, 6S 8000 mAh Li-ion ~1 kg (see batteries-small/large research).

Stack / board patterns: 16x16 (M2/M3 micro boards; O3 adapter plates exist for 20x20 -> 16x16), 20x20 (M2, or M3/M4 holes with rubber grommets down to M2), 25.5x25.5 (whoop AIOs and most whoop/1S digital VTXs), 30.5x30.5 (M3, 5in and up). A smaller board on a larger pattern needs an adapter plate; a larger board will not fit a smaller pattern.

Digital VTX patterns: O4 25.5x25.5 (RDQ; DJI FAQ loosely says '30 x 30 mm'); O4 Pro 20x20 or 25.5x25.5; O3 25.5x25.5; Vista 20x20; Walksnail Pro/V2/Moonlight/GT/GT2 20x20 or 25.5x25.5; Walksnail Nano Kit V3 25.5x25.5 (M2) or 20x20 (M3 holes); Walksnail Mini 1S 25.5x25.5; HDZero Race V3 (M4 grommeted) and Freestyle V2 20x20; HDZero Whoop V2/Lite/ECO 25.5x25.5; Wyvern Link 25.5 (Alpha V2 also 20x20); WiFiLink 2 25.5x25.5.

Motor patterns by stator: 0702-0802 whoop motors use the whoop (W1S) 1S pattern with 1 mm shafts; 1002-1102 (and some 1103) use the 3-hole 6.6 mm micro pattern with 1.5 mm shafts; 1103/1104/1202.5/1204/1303/1404 and T-Motor P1604 use 9x9 M2; 1507/1804/2004/2105.5/2205 use 12x12 M2 (some 3.6in frames list 12x12 for 14xx-class motors); 2207/2306/2306.5/2506/2507 use 16x16 M3; 2806.5/2807/2810/3110/3115/3220 use 19x19 M3 (a few 2306s, e.g. EMAX E3, also 19x19); X-class 4214/4215/5215 use 30x30 M4 (some 25x25).
Shafts/hubs: whoop props press onto 1 mm (0702/0802) or 1.5 mm (1002-1404) shafts; 1.5in-2.5in class 2004/1604 motors often use T-mount; 5in and larger use M5 threaded shafts; X-class motors use M6.
Camera widths: nano 14 mm, micro 19 mm, mini 22 mm, full 28 mm. Most 3in-5in frames are sized for 19 mm micro cameras (fpvknowitall); many 5in-7in frames also take 20 mm DJI/O3 cameras.

Digital camera widths: DJI O4 module 13.44 x 12.36 mm -> 14 mm nano slots via O4 adapter plates/cases or Flywoo 18/20 mm shells; DJI O4 Pro 20 mm wide but 25.55 mm deep and 23.3 mm tall; DJI O3 20 mm (frames list '20mm (DJI and O3 camera)'); Walksnail Pro/V2/GT/GT2 cameras 19 mm (Moonlight 19.6 x 19 x 24 mm); Walksnail Mini 1S / Nano V3 / Lite cameras 14 mm; HDZero Nano V3/Lux/Eco/Nano 90 14 mm (Nano V3 and Lux are listed L14 x W16 x H14; Nano 90 ships with a 19 mm bracket in the Freestyle V2 kit); HDZero Micro V3 19 mm; OpenIPC IMX415 modules on WiFiLink 2 and Wyvern Alpha V2 19 mm (Wyvern 200 mW camera size unpublished; its 100 mW Alpha sibling lists 14 mm).
Adapter plates bridge O4 cameras into O3/19-20 mm mounts (e.g. Brain3D O4-to-O3 adapter, Lumenier O4 adapter plates, Flywoo O4 Wide-Angle Lens 'O3 / 20mm' shell).

1S whoops: PH2.0 supports only 4.5 A continuous; BT2.0 and GNB27 support 9 A continuous / 15 A burst; A30 15 A standard / 30 A peak (Gaoneng listing). BT2.0 'gives significantly lower resistance ... and less voltage drop' than even solid-pin PH2.0 (fpvknowitall). Fly on the drone's native plug - adapters are fine for charging only.
Toothpicks and 2-4S micros: 'XT30 is the best all-around choice'; GNB27 saves weight; avoid PH2.0 (fpvknowitall). Flywoo/DeepSpace 2-3in BNFs ship with XT30.

3S-6S 5in-10in: XT60 is on 'about 95%' of 220-size quads (GetFPV). Amass XT60H: 0.8 mOhm, 60 A rated / 100 A max, 3.5 g each per GetFPV (not re-fetchable; HTTP 403). Some 3.5in 6S cinewhoops (CineApe 35, Axisflying C35) already use XT60.

10in+, cinelifters and X-class: XT90 (the RDQ-listed XT90 V2 is 50 A rated / 90 A max - note this is lower than the XT60H figure above because the two come from different vendors' rating methods) and AS150/XT150 (150 A) - e.g. Lumenier CineLifter and Tattu G-Tech packs ship with AS150 or XT90-S.
XT30 current rating was not stated on the listings checked; treat it as the step below XT60.

FC-ESC 8-pin harnesses: usually JST-SH 1.0 mm on ESCs, sometimes JST-GH on the FC side (Lumenier LUX H743 includes GH-to-SH 8-pin cables). Same plug, different wire order between brands: Lumenier ESCs are VBAT, GND, CURR, TLM, M1, M2, M3, M4; Flywoo GOKU 406S is GND, BAT, M1, M2, M3, M4, CUR; iFlight BLITZ Mini F4 prints CUR/M4/M3/M2/M1/BAT/G. A straight cable between mismatched brands can put battery voltage on a signal or ground pin, so compare both pinouts and re-pin the cable (or solder) when they differ. Same-brand stacks ship with a matching cable.
Octo/X8 setups: FCs like the Matek H7A3-SLIM provide two 8-pin ESC ports for two 4-in-1 ESCs.

HD VTX power/data: HDZero Whoop V2 ships with a 'Betaflight standard digital VTX plug' harness; Walksnail GT2 uses a JST1.0 6-pin power cable; Walksnail Nano V3 uses JST1.0 4-pin power; DJI O3/O4 use DJI's 3-in-1 cable; some FCs (e.g. SpeedyBee AIO F4) plug straight into O3/Vista/RunCam Link without re-pinning - check the FC's HD connector pinout before plugging in.
